faqs.a: Yes. The City of Florence requires a plumbing permit and a safety inspection for all water heater replacements, so the installation complies with current Alabama safety codes. Our team manages the entire permit and inspection process on your behalf.
faqs.q: Is a permit required for a water heater replacement in Florence, AL?

faqs.a: Active supply line leaks, overflowing toilets, leaking water heaters, and main sewer line backups are all plumbing emergencies. If you have an active leak, turn your main water shutoff valve clockwise to stop the water, then turn off the breaker or gas valve for your water heater - that stabilizes your property while we dispatch a technician.
faqs.q: What counts as a plumbing emergency, and what should I do while I wait?

faqs.a: Replace it if the inner lining is leaking or the system is over ten years old - structural rust inside the tank cannot be fixed. Minor failures like a bad heating element or thermostat can usually be repaired, but if your unit needs multiple service calls or stops providing consistent hot water, upgrading is usually the most cost-effective option.
faqs.q: Should I repair or replace my water heater?
